title: Revision of Pronoun, a Mentor Prompt
author: Terry Yu
summary: Terry Yu shares a revised AI mentor prompt called 'Pronoun,' designed to help writing students explore how pronoun choice shapes rhetoric and reader relationship. The prompt creates a chatbot persona that guides students through three narrative perspectives—third person, second person, and first person—using a consistent scenario to make the rhetorical differences tangible. The approach is grounded in empirical research on using AI to generate mentor texts for ESL learners, where AI's ability to analyze linguistic patterns and generate appropriately leveled example texts makes it well-suited for writing instruction. Yu builds the prompt around the concepts of interiority (access to a character's thoughts and feelings) and exteriority (observable actions and events only), teaching students to recognize the demands and constraints each point of view places on writer and reader. The prompt includes metacognitive scaffolding: the Pronoun persona monitors for moments when students reverse a line of thinking or express confusion, turning those incidents into instructional opportunities. A practical activation tip is included: users must open the chat with 'I'd like to have a chat with Pronoun' to prevent AI system prompts from treating the mentor prompt as a jailbreak attempt.
points: The Pronoun AI persona guides students through first-, second-, and third-person narration of the same scenario, making the rhetorical differences concrete—first person expresses full interiority (the writer's thoughts and feelings); third person expresses full exteriority (observable facts only).

The prompt's design is grounded in a published empirical study on using AI to generate bespoke mentor texts for ESL learners, where AI's ability to analyze user language and generate appropriately leveled example texts makes it effective for writing instruction.

Metacognitive scaffolding is embedded in the prompt: the Pronoun persona identifies and names specific moments when students shift direction, reverse thinking, or express confusion—turning those incidents into teachable metacognitive opportunities.
quotes: I’ve worked my way through the original Pronoun prompt several times now, posing as a student, making changes in background, intent, and specific actions along the way.

Cut and paste it into an AI. Prompt “I’d like to have a chat with Pronoun.” You need to open the chat in this way to prevent the SYSTEM prompt from deciphering this prompt as an attempt at a jail break.
AI is suited for this work because it can analyze linguistic patterns in user’s input language and then generate interesting and appropriately leveled text for learner’s to read and emulate.
Interiority is having access to what another intelligent entity is thinking and feeling. Thoughts and feelings equate roughly with sentience, human consciousness.
Strong third person exteriority is having access only to the surrounding world outside the thoughts of anyone. Observations, reports, instructions, and the like, are strong third person.
The key is teaching students to recognize what demands are placed on the writer and what constraints are placed on readers by virtue of choice of point of view.
